note: First campaign: RSKj perf-lab/integration vs rustock (Lerner fork + harness branches), Docker on this Mac.

docker/ecdsa.why: rustock faster in 6/6 cycles, median -60.78%, sign-test p=0.03125

docker/mainnet-sim.why: rustock faster in 0/6 cycles, median +220.76%, sign-test p=0.03125

config._doc: rsk-clients-lab settings. Read by bin/*.py and bin/*.sh. README.md explains the method.

mainnet-sim.description: k6 option 14 (mainnet-sim): storage writes, ERC-20, native transfers and calldata-heavy rollup txs, about 164 txs per block

ecdsa.description: k6 option 7 (CPU ECDSA): signature-recovery-heavy contract calls, almost all of each block is transaction execution

machines._doc: Locks shared with rsk-perf-lab in ~/.research-lab/locks (bin/lib.sh). A campaign holds this Mac's Docker slot as a long holder, so perf-lab's short replays and gates go first.

rskj._doc: RSKj in the harness. Measured at the head of perf-lab/integration (everything rsk-perf-lab has proven), recorded per campaign.
rskj.settings: conf/rskj/rsk.conf (rskip144 off, rskip97 at 0), conf/rskj/logback.xml, -Xms2G -Xmx4G, flushNumberOfBlocks 10

rustock._doc: rustock in the harness. Built from the harness adapter branch until its upstream pull requests merge. import_args: rskj's regtest chain as the lab's rsk.conf sets it (genesis file, rskip97=0, rskj's gas-limit bounds, skipPowValidation), the trie in its own RocksDB (a fresh data dir with the default single backend is refused by the fork), flush every {flush} blocks like RSKj.
